artifacts.summary: 4-phase plan: jq default-not-force fix at both config.json write sites, a pre-claudeSettings injection-hook detector, doc/comment updates, and an on-machine rebuild plus forced vendor-update verification.

memory_candidates.content: A detection guard that inspects mutable state which an enforcing writer in the same run resets is structurally dead code, and it looks like a working check. In home-manager, dotfiles.nix's claudeSettings activation entry lists 'hooks' in its enforced-key jq merge, so it replaces ~/.claude/settings.json's hooks array from the repo source on every switch. A guard declared entryAfter [ writeBoundary claudeSettings ] therefore always reads an already-cleaned file and can never observe the injection it exists to detect. The general rule: when ordering a detector against a repairer that share one mutable target, the detector must run BEFORE the repairer. That ordering then changes the abort-vs-warn decision too -- aborting before the repairer forfeits the automatic repair and leaves the bad state in place, so a loud non-fatal report plus the repairer's own strip gives detection and repair in one pass, while the hard-failing exit belongs in a standalone invocation that cannot block the switch.
